issues.detail: The Hebrew 'שְׂפַת יֶתֶר' means 'excellent/lofty speech' or 'arrogant speech' (literally 'lip of excess/surplus'), not '過多的嘴唇' (excessive lips). The Chinese rendering changes the meaning from a quality of speech to a physical quantity of lips.

The Hebrew 'לְנָדִיב' means 'to a noble/generous person' (from the root נדב, meaning noble, willing, princely), not '高傲人' (haughty/proud person). This swaps the subject from a noble person to a proud person, changing the verse's claim.
